user_prompt_en:
I'm trying to put together a website for a new boutique translation agency I'm starting with a few colleagues. We mainly handle corporate legal documents and specialized literary translations, so the site needs to hold a lot of detailed information without making the visitor feel overwhelmed. Right off the bat, I want the whole page on a dark ground with light text on it. That is non-negotiable for me, I just think it looks so much sleeker and more serious for this kind of business. At the very top, we just need a simple text logo on the left and a few links to jump around the page on the right. Below that, a big welcome area that says something like "Bridging Languages, Connecting Worlds" with a short paragraph underneath explaining our core mission and our commitment to absolute accuracy.

Right below the welcome area, I want a large section to list out our actual translation services, like technical document translation, live corporate interpretation, software localization, and certified legal transcripts. For how this part is actually put together on the screen, I was looking at that Chinese text tool interface, the one with all those light grey panels. I'd love it if we could arrange our services exactly like that—breaking all the different offerings up into several soft, rounded rectangular panels that sit tightly packed next to and on top of each other, almost like a compact dashboard. Each panel would hold a different service category, a short description, and a list of the specific industries we cater to for that service.

After the services, we need a clear step-by-step section explaining our workflow to new clients, moving from the initial quote request to document review, the actual translation, and the final native-speaker proofreading stage. Because it's going to be quite a bit of reading, the letters themselves really need to carry the visual weight. I really love the text treatment on that page with the blue top and the huge beige spaces. Please make our words behave just like that—using those massive, super thick modern headings that create a huge, striking contrast right next to really tiny, fine paragraph text. And if you could mix in just a little bit of that classic, older-looking book font they used for some of the smaller accent words or quotes, that would be perfect. It makes the reading experience so much more engaging.

Finally, the bottom of the page has to be a comprehensive contact and quote request area. Clients will need to type in their name, company, select the type of document from a dropdown menu, and hit a big submit button. While we are building out these input areas and buttons, I want to make sure we stay far away from the style on that page with the thick black bar across the top. I really dislike how heavy that top bar feels, and I definitely don't want those standard pure blue buttons with the little icons, or those dotted lines they used to split things up. Instead of all that clunky stuff, I just want really clean, flat input fields and buttons that are basically just thin outlines that gently fill in with a solid color when you mouse over them. Just keep it quiet and unobtrusive.

Since a lot of our initial inquiries come from people browsing on their commutes, the whole thing needs to shrink down perfectly for phone screens. The top links should tuck away into a simple menu, and all those tightly packed dashboard blocks of services should naturally just stack up one by one in a single column so people can easily scroll straight down to the contact form at the bottom.

user_prompt_zh:
本次迭代我们要为一家新设立的心理咨询工作室上线一个对外的官方展示单页。从业务侧来看，这个站点的核心诉求是向潜在来访者传递高度专业、克制且极具安全感的机构形象，虽然是一个静态单页、结构简单，但每一个展现细节都关乎用户的预约转化率。前期的表现形式我已经确定好了，整页底色我要深的，字浮在深底上，这一点没有任何讨论空间，必须严格按照这个底色来做。为了适应目前多端触达的场景，这次上线的验收标准之一就是严格的响应式，页面在手机端和电脑端两端都要绝对好看，不能有任何因为屏幕缩放导致的文字挤压或模块错位问题。

在空间的处理上，我觉得那个有竖排中文的档案页特别契合心理咨询需要的留白感。我们要它那种独特的非对称疏散做法，一侧固定有极大的竖排标题作为每个业务区域的引导，主体内容则是以极高留白的错落列表和非传统网格来展现，让来访者一进来就能感觉视觉在这个空间里是能深呼吸的。文字的表现力方面，我希望呈现出浓厚的传统纸质报纸或学术文献气质。关于字里的具体细节，你看那个米底衬线体英文页，就全篇使用类似的古典衬线字体，字号对比适中，行距要给得非常宽松。我们要让来访者在阅读那些心理学科普和咨询师介绍时，有一种安静翻阅专业书籍的沉浸感。

页面顶部的首屏区域，我们要放工作室的品牌愿景“在幽暗处见光”，下面紧跟一个初次预约评估的行动入口。这里涉及到的具体区块，比如预约动作和数据展示，就参考首屏带深色横幅的企业站里的处理方式，做成那种具有明确边界的网页区块，采用直角纯色填充的按钮，以及用线型图标和数字构成的统计模块，用这种干净利落的形式来展示我们工作室成立的年份、累计咨询小时数和擅长的流派数量。

首屏往下滚动会进入咨询师团队介绍区域，这里需要交代首席咨询师的受训背景、督导经历和临床专长，大段的履历文字正好能发挥前面提到的宽松行距优势。紧接着是服务范围与收费标准，这块要交代清楚个体咨询、伴侣咨询和团体沙盘的具体价格段次。考虑到初次寻求心理帮助的来访者往往有较多顾虑，我们在页面中下部必须放一个常见问题解答区域，说明诸如保密原则的例外情况、取消预约的退费规定以及首次危机干预的流程等。这个功能点需要做成折叠展开的形式，用户点一下某个具体问题，完整的解答文案才会在下方平滑地展开显示。页面最底部是常规的联系方式、机构详细地址、乘车指引以及一条全国心理危机干预热线的24小时常驻提示。整个页面的文案方向要始终体现出心理学专家的职业伦理与人文温度，请确保交付的代码逻辑清晰，各部分内容平滑衔接，以便我们能顺利完成上线前的功能验收。

user_prompt_en:
For the upcoming Northbound suite, I need a robust, responsive QR code generator interface that strictly locks to a single viewport height with zero scrolling, lifting its entire visual syntax and three-column spatial rhythm directly from the screens provided.
- Set up the macro-layout exactly as shown: a deep gray structural background with dual dark sidebars flanking that distinct, spacious beige central canvas where the actual QR preview will sit, maintaining the calm, low-density atmosphere.
- Build out a robust configuration form in the left panel switching between URL, WiFi, and vCard inputs, utilizing the exact micro-ui elements visible in your reference—specifically those thin-stroked rounded buttons, the subtle checkboxes, and the delicate sliders with circular thumbs to control QR dot scale and margin padding.
- Port over the typographic hierarchy and metric displays for the right-hand panel, keeping the extremely large tracking numbers and those tiny keyboard shortcut cards to show real-time scan estimates and file format options (PNG/SVG).
- Anchor the color logic to what's in the images, using those exact low-saturation yellow and blue accents for progress states or active toggles, ensuring the visual weight of the active state pops just enough against the dark UI without disrupting the overall contrast ratios.
- Implement snappy, immediate hover state transitions across all interactive controls and ensure the layout gracefully condenses its grid logic on smaller viewports while preserving the strict one-screen constraint and alignment spacing.

by_label.B: 页面顶部是全宽的深色背景图导航区，主体内容严格遵循传统的两栏布局：左侧为宽泛的图文列表列，右侧为较窄的侧边栏模块。
by_label.C: 典型的技术文档结构，带有左侧固定的文本目录导航栏，右侧则是占据主要屏幕空间的单列、居中对齐的大段图文内容流。

layout.why: 第3份（C）的左目录右单列长文结构属于专用的文档排版，与前两份偏向资讯博客的多列图文排版截然不同。

by_label.A: 页面以大面积的纯白色为底，使用高明度的薄荷绿（翠绿）作为唯一的强调色和品牌色（Logo、按钮、图形装饰线条），辅以极浅的灰色用于划分区块。
by_label.B: 包含深紫灰色的顶部大图背景，主体部分为白底，使用偏灰暗的砖红色或珊瑚粉色作为按钮的主色调。
by_label.C: 极致的黑白灰文档配色，仅在个别按钮或提示框背景上使用了标准的系统蓝色作为功能性点缀。

palette.why: 第1份（A）通篇贯穿的亮眼薄荷绿作为唯一核心点缀色，这一色彩特征非常明确，极易辨认是否模仿了它。

by_label.A: 现代感强烈的无衬线字体，字号反差极大（首页顶部有巨大字号的标语），标题使用了较粗的字重，信息层级非常跳跃抢眼。
by_label.B: 整体偏向细体的无衬线排版，标题和正文字重都不大，正文采用了较浅的灰色和较宽的行距，营造出安静的长文阅读感。
by_label.C: 极其基础的系统级无衬线字体，缺乏装饰性，各级标题与正文的字号差距不大，类似未加深度CSS修饰的默认网页文本或Markdown输出。

typography.why: 第3份（C）的字体排版极具“原生默认”感，既没有第1份的现代夸张字号，也没有第2份的轻盈细体设定。

by_label.A: 大量使用两端为半圆的胶囊形状按钮（包含实心填充和细描边样式），文章内容被包裹在有明确边界的卡片中，页面上还有空心几何方块等装饰组件。
by_label.B: 文章列表项没有卡片容器，直接以图文形式在白底上堆叠；主要的交互按钮为微圆角的矩形，采用单一纯色填充且无阴影；配图多为直角或极小的圆角。
by_label.C: 组件极少，仅有非常基础的小圆角纯色按钮，以及带有淡色背景和纯色边框的系统级信息提示框（Alert）。

component.why: 第2份（B）的扁平小圆角矩形按钮和完全去卡片化（无边界）的文章列表排版，与第1份的胶囊按钮及卡片堆叠差异显著。

by_label.A: 活泼生动，具有较强的生活气息与轻松随性的感觉。
by_label.B: 相对传统稳重，呈现出偏正式、安静的图文阅读氛围。
by_label.C: 极其克制、冷峻，呈现出高度理性和干瘪的纯粹工具/文档气质。

user_prompt_en:
**Overview**
As a community organizer for a volunteer-run civic data collective, I need us to build a slow query monitoring panel. Our public database has been timing out during high-traffic events, and our volunteer database administrators need a dedicated view to identify bottlenecks. Because we operate on a shoestring budget, this needs to be a highly efficient, single-page application. I want the information to be painfully clear and strictly accessible to all our volunteers, including those using screen readers or relying on keyboard navigation.

**Page structure**
This tool needs to present a lot of data without overwhelming the user. I actively do not want the layout to end up like that dashboard with the dark left navigation (the second set of screenshots) or the job board with the fixed left sidebar and right-side feed (the fourth set of images). We do not need persistent navigation sidebars eating up our horizontal screen space for a single-focus tool. Instead, I want a wide, top-down full-bleed structure. It should start with a commanding full-width header, flow into a large data visualization area taking up the top half of the viewport, and then stack a full-width feed of the problematic queries underneath.

**Visual**
For the typography, I want exactly what is happening in the first few screenshots (the black and white grid page). Give me those massive, ultra-heavy sans-serif headers that practically shout at you, and keep the actual data and body text in a small, dense, tightly packed sans-serif. Use heavy uppercase letters to create an extreme, aggressive contrast between the section titles and the granular details.

The whole page needs to feel like that same black-and-white grid site: completely clinical, restrained, and like a highly rational, serious technical manual. There should be absolutely no redundant emotional decoration—just cold, hard facts so our team feels the urgency of the performance issues.

When it comes to the colors, please avoid the palette from that third site (the archival one with the vintage parchment look). That warm beige background, brown text, and retro olive tagging is far too low-contrast and nostalgic for a modern monitoring tool. Instead, give me a harsh, high-contrast monochrome foundation—pure white backgrounds with absolute black text—and introduce just one incredibly sharp, accessible accent color (like a vibrant magenta or electric cyan) specifically to highlight critical alerts and data chart lines.

**Component design**
For the individual slow query cards, the filter inputs, and the action buttons, let's borrow the look of the small blocks from that last set of screenshots (the one with the bright orange blocks overlapping the big photo). I love how substantial those are. Give our query cards that same large, sharp-edged, right-angled solid color box treatment. We can even have the primary filter panel slightly overlap the bottom of the main data graph, similar to how those blocks sit over the background image. For the lists of execution statistics inside these cards, use those prominent, single-color vector icons to anchor each line item clearly.

**Interaction**
The top half of the page will be heavily interactive. I need a complex brushing timeline where volunteers can click and drag over a specific time window on a line chart to filter the query feed below. When a user clicks on a specific query block in the feed, a stateful side-panel should slide in from the right edge containing a flame graph of the query execution plan. This requires smooth transition animations, but we must implement logic to immediately disable these animations if the user's system requests reduced motion.

**Data & Copy**
The content volume will be substantial and split evenly: about half text (raw SQL strings, execution metadata, and maintainer notes) and half image/canvas (flame graphs, time series charts for execution times, memory usage gauges).
*   The main header should simply read "SYSTEM HEALTH: QUERY LATENCY".
*   The graph tooltips should display specific metrics: "95th Percentile Execution: 1.2s", "Index Miss Rate: 84%".
*   The feed should open with a direct, helpful summary: "Detected 43 queries exceeding the 500ms threshold in the selected window."
*   Each query card must display the truncated SQL text, total time locked, and rows examined. The tone must remain totally objective and supportive.
*   Let's ensure the data blocks also include historical comparison text. For example, include small helper text under the main metrics saying, "Compared to the 7-day moving average, lock contention has increased by 14%." This helps contextualize the raw numbers for our junior volunteers who might not immediately know what constitutes a bad metric.
*   Include an input area in the expanded state where maintainers can leave plain-text notes for each other, like "Adding a composite index on user_id and created_at resolved this on staging."

**Acceptance**
*   The text contrast ratios must exceed WCAG AAA standards across the board.
*   The interactive data visualizations (brushing, zooming) must have keyboard fallback controls.
*   The page must be delivered as a single HTML file containing all structural markup, scoped CSS, and the necessary JavaScript to simulate the stateful interactions and render the mock charts.
*   The interface must remain perfectly usable at a 200% zoom level without elements overlapping.
*   Ensure all vector icons used in the query cards are paired with visually hidden text for screen readers.
*   The slide-over panel must trap focus while open and close gracefully when the Escape key is pressed.

by_label.A: 严格的水平和垂直网格实线分割的满屏布局，信息密度高，多栏并排，像老式报纸排版。
by_label.B: 经典的后台全屏布局，左侧固定深色导航栏，顶部顶栏，右侧主区域为多张卡片组成的流式网格。
by_label.C: 居中的单列长文档式布局，阅读区宽度固定，两侧大面积留白，内容按章节向下堆叠。
by_label.D: 居中定宽的两栏布局，左侧为较窄的筛选表单栏，右侧为较宽的卡片列表信息流，顶部有居中的导航条。
by_label.E: 传统的企业官网通栏布局，顶部全宽大图，下方主内容区包裹在一个定宽的白色容器内并叠在浅色背景底纹上。

layout.why: 第 2 份是典型的“左侧固定深色导航+右侧卡片网格”全屏后台布局（图4）；第 4 份是典型的“左侧窄栏筛选表单+右侧宽栏卡片列表”的居中网页布局（图10），两者的页面结构特征都非常明确且互不相同。

by_label.A: 黑白极简对比，大面积白色底色配黑色文字和粗线，仅有极少量的土褐色/暗橄榄色作为局部小点缀。
by_label.B: 极浅的灰白色网页底色，纯白面板，深灰色文字，以亮蓝色作为侧边栏选中状态等交互元素的主色。
by_label.C: 偏暖的米黄/羊皮纸色底色，深灰/褐色文字，搭配复古的暗橄榄绿、土黄色标签和表头，整体呈现复古做旧的暖色调。
by_label.D: 纯白底色，浅灰分割线，深灰色文字，使用明亮的标准蓝色作为按钮和关键交互链接的主色调，色彩清爽现代。
by_label.E: 以亮橙色为绝对的主导视觉强调色，搭配深色实景照片背景和浅灰色暗纹底底色，反差强烈。

palette.why: 第 3 份具有非常强烈的米黄色/羊皮纸底色和做旧暖色调（暗绿/土黄）特征，与其他几份纯白或浅灰底色的现代现代风格对比极其鲜明（图7/9）。

by_label.A: 极其醒目的无衬线粗体大字作为标题（类似 Impact 字体），正文使用较小且密集的无衬线字体，大写字母较多，字号和字重层级对比极端。
by_label.B: 标准常规的现代 UI 无衬线字体，字重和字号层级变化平缓，侧重信息可读性。
by_label.C: 标题和正文多用优雅的衬线体，而在数据、表格和日志部分则混排了等宽/打字机风格的字体。
by_label.D: 圆润友好的现代几何无衬线字体，字号层级清晰，数字和特定标签有专门加粗。
by_label.E: 大标题使用传统的衬线字体，正文使用行距较大的无衬线字体。

typography.why: 第 1 份使用了极具视觉冲击力的超粗无衬线大字标题和全大写的密集正文排版，与其他几份常规、圆润或复古的字体风格截然不同（图1/2/3）。

by_label.D: 典型的现代 Web 组件，卡片带有明显的圆角和极浅的边框；输入框有圆角；主按钮是完全圆角（胶囊形）的实心色块，并大量使用圆角药丸形标签。

user_prompt_en:
**Overview**
This PRD outlines the requirements for a new seismic record browser, designed for structural engineers and researchers to monitor and evaluate tectonic activity. The goal is to provide a highly functional tool that still feels incredibly refined and luxurious. It needs to present dense scientific data clearly without ever overwhelming the user.

**Page structure**
At the top of the viewport, we need an asymmetric split. Place the primary search controls and introductory text on the left, and a large visual element—like a live waveform preview or epicenter map—on the right. This arrangement should work just like the top section of that dark blog with the cyan text. Below this initial view, display the recent seismic events arranged in a regular, multi-column grid of cards, matching how the lower half of that same dark blog is organized.

**Visuals**
For the color choices, I want the extreme restraint seen in the densely packed data report. Use a pure white background with pure black text and structural lines. There should be absolutely zero colored elements on the screen to maintain a stark, clinical elegance. 
For the text styling, use a clean sans-serif. Make the main event titles massively oversized and bold, creating a sharp contrast against tiny, grey descriptive text. This treatment should match how the text looks on the dark blog with the cyan headers.

**Interaction**
The interface elements should follow what is shown on the dark blue page with the red gradient button. Specifically, use pure white cards with distinct, heavy drop shadows to lift them off the background. All buttons must be fully rounded, pill-shaped forms. Any text inputs for filtering the earthquake data should be minimalist, showing only the bottom border line.
Clicking any event card in the grid must trigger a smooth inline expansion, pushing the other cards aside to reveal a detailed, stateful interactive seismograph view without forcing a page reload.

**Acceptance**
- The structural arrangement must not break when printed to standard A4 paper; the grid should gracefully adjust to fit the printed page width without cutting off data.
- The interface must meet strict accessibility standards, ensuring every text input and expanded state is fully keyboard reachable.
- The contrast ratio of the text must remain extremely high, relying entirely on the black, white, and grey scales requested.

user_prompt_en:
I am putting together a new membership benefits page for our enterprise documentation hub, and I need a precise, well-structured interface to handle a lot of technical information. The page needs to feature a stateful view, specifically an interactive toggle that switches the displayed content between standard and enterprise tier features dynamically. The flow should start with a clear value proposition, transition into the pricing toggle, present a dense grid detailing API rate limits and support SLAs, include a collapsible FAQ area, and end with a contact form for custom SLA deployments.

To organize all this, structure the interface with a fixed sidebar on the left occupying roughly a third of the viewport, leaving the main content on the right to scroll independently and house a two-column grid for the tier benefits. This left-right split is how space is managed on the one with the dark sidebar, which handles density beautifully. For the colors, I want exactly what is used on the watch page with the orange buttons. I want that pure white background and deep dark grey text, deploying that highly saturated orange-yellow gradient exclusively for our primary subscription toggle and checkout buttons to ensure they stand out completely from the technical text.

For the individual interface elements, they must remain understated. The feature blocks should be handled like the cards on that dark sidebar page, meaning they act as simple containers featuring very tiny rounded corners, entirely omitting any structural outer borders or drop shadows. Any secondary interaction points, like search inputs or minor links, must be thin grey wireframe outlines with zero background fill. Completely separate from those visual references, I require the main body text to be set in a classic serif typeface featuring distinct thin and thick strokes, to give the dense copy a formal, editorial quality.

user_prompt_en: We are initiating the development of the main portal for our upcoming Global AI Hackathon Showcase. The core user value here is to provide a seamless discovery experience for developers exploring past winning algorithms and team submissions. To meet our acceptance criteria, the page needs clearly delineated functional areas: an overarching introductory header, an immersive stateful data visualization block for live scoring brackets, a dynamic project gallery, and a final registration block for the winter sequence. For how the page is put together, look at the site with the large photos and the dark top; I want the content blocked out exactly like that, featuring a massive, full-width hero area with a big background image, followed by main body sections arranged in asymmetrical two-column splits where text anchors one side and media sits on the other. However, the colors need to come from the support page with the massive blue header. We will use that deep royal blue as the dominant background color for the top half of the screen, keeping the main content area pure white with dark grey text, utilizing the deep blue solely as a high-contrast accent. From that same blue support page, I need the exact treatment of the smaller elements: give me that giant pill-shaped pure white input field for our project search, and build the gallery using those borderless white floating cards with the soft diffuse shadows, incorporating the dark blue wireframe icons and sharp right-angle solid buttons. One technical requirement that is already finalized internally is the font choice; the main body text must absolutely be set in a classic serif typeface with distinct thin-thick strokes to give the technical data an editorial feel. The final deliverable must ensure the stateful filtering transitions feel instantaneous across all these blocks.

user_prompt_zh:
我是做数据分析的，近期我们「无声电台」项目为了提升留存率，准备新上一个浏览器小游戏聚合页。页面呈现对数据转化很关键，我想参考后面米白色背景带粗黑线的造船页里那套文字处理方式，就要那种极其粗壮醒目的无衬线大字做标题，字粗细对比极其强烈，拉出一种很强的海报或复古老报纸的张力。底板这块我已经决定了，整页底色我要深的，所有的字要直接浮在这个深色底上，让数字和图表更抓眼。

页面顶端留一个基础的导航栏方便切换品类。中间核心是游戏入口矩阵，这片区域我觉得中间那个深色图标展示页处理得挺对味，内容高度居中收拢、紧凑得很，你就也照那意思给弄个三列或两列的小型方块网格阵列，接着在阵列正下方紧挨着放一个代码区块，展示数据调用的接口。至于网格里的小游戏卡片，我看上了最前头黄蓝主色活动网站里的细节，卡片图片左上角也要直接叠加一个醒目的纯黄底色方块，正好用来标示游戏通关率。

底下再留个订阅新游内测的表单。表单的输入框和按钮也顺着前头那个黄蓝活动页里的做法，全做成直角且完全扁平的。最后补一段根据设备宽度自动折叠适配的周榜数据区，以可读和方便玩家自行筛选为准。

user_prompt_zh: 大家好，我们是“两只鹿”社区公益组织，最近要上线一门面向街坊的在线课程，想请你搭个详情页。考虑受众有不少中老年群体，信息必须清楚。网页的页面划分我希望参考那个带粗黑边框和粉色大色块的网页，用黑色实粗线切分出不对齐的方块区域，把密集的数据表格也妥当塞进去，看着规整利落。颜色去拿首屏黑底配黄字那个网页的，底色铺深灰色，用它里面特别抓眼的明黄色做主色和强调色，让重点非常醒目。字体的感觉去抓带紫色波浪头图的那个网页，板块的大标题用极粗的大号现代衬线体，跟普通无衬线正文形成极大的粗细对比，这种层次感对长辈很友好。至于具体的卡片和输入框，千万别学多张蓝色手机UI图，也别碰全黑底色博客那个，我不要泛泛的弥散阴影和柔和圆角，也不要毫无边界感贴在背景上的纯平暗灰矩形，我们就老老实实做成边缘锐利、带高对比实线的硬朗框子。内容上开篇先放课程名和一段带多节点折叠展开的互动式大纲，方便查阅大块目标。往下排讲师区，带出大字号寄语。接着是费用块，包含全价和减免价的动态状态切换。最后加个轻量的数据可视化区块，点亮当前学习的成员分布图即可。一切以实用为主。

user_prompt_en:
Hello there. I am organizing community programs for a non-profit initiative we run called Amber Works, and I am looking to put together a local events calendar to share our upcoming weekend activities. We are on a very tight budget, so I want to keep this build extremely simple—just a static single page that gives families all the information they need without any complicated bells and whistles. Our main audience for this specific board will be primary school students and their parents, so accessibility and clear, straightforward communication are my absolute top priorities. I was looking at the design you have pulled up here, and I actually think it provides a wonderful starting point for us, even though it looks quite sophisticated for a kids' page at first glance.

I would like to basically use the exact layout and color scheme you are showing me in these screens. That deep, dark background paired with the bright orange accents works perfectly—we can frame it like a cool "night sky and bright stars" theme, which the kids will really enjoy. Please keep the page structure exactly as it is, with those nicely spaced, centered cards for the main feed and that capsule-shaped floating menu fixed at the bottom of the screen. I especially want to keep the component styling from your example, like the large soft rounded corners on the cards with no harsh borders, and that great little interaction where the bottom menu icons get a bright orange circular background when you hover over them. That immediate visual feedback is fantastic for our younger users who are still learning to navigate the web.

However, we definitely need to adapt the typography to better suit our young audience. Please keep the clean spacing and the clear visual hierarchy between the titles and the body paragraphs, but change the actual typeface to something much rounder, larger, and friendlier. The text needs to be highly legible for young readers, using slightly thicker weights and generous line height so they never lose their place while reading. I do really love those giant orange starting letters at the beginning of the paragraphs in the detailed reading view you are showing, so let's carry that specific typographic idea over, just using our new, friendlier font choice.

As for the page contents, let's start at the very top with a simple, welcoming title for the Amber Works activity board. Below that, we will flow straight into the upcoming events using those centered cards. Each card should feature a fun, bright photo taking up the top half, and the bottom half will hold the event title, the date, and a very short, plain-English summary, like "Community Garden Planting" or "Recycled Art Workshop." When a child clicks on one of these activity cards, I want it to transition into a detailed view exactly like the one in your reference, where a large, full-width image sits at the top and a single narrow column of text follows directly below it.

For these detailed event descriptions, we need to maintain a very balanced layout, keeping it strictly about fifty percent text and fifty percent images so the kids do not get intimidated by huge walls of reading. To make the visual side even more engaging, I need you to build in a specific extra feature: whenever someone clicks on any of the pictures inside the event description text, it should pop open to show a full-sized, high-resolution gallery view of the image. This will let them look closely at the crafts we will be making or the places we will be visiting. Overall, just keep the spacious, focused, and quiet atmosphere of the design you have there, but soften the edges with our kid-friendly text so they feel right at home discovering their next big weekend adventure.

user_prompt_zh: 搞个乐队新专发布页，顶部带响应式导航，下面顺着铺开主视觉、试听片段、套餐档位的横向对比以及底部的预购表单。交付要求必须能纯离线跑绝对不许挂任何外链资源。这个内容区我要左右两栏并排着看，背景和字色直接吸最前面那个黑底细线页面的，极暗深灰底加白灰字，强调色就用那上面的暗黄绿，标题和正文比例抠中间那个带红黄蓝大色块的模板，用极粗巨型无衬线主标加底下短实线，副标全大写距拉大，正文留足行高。另外容器和表单样式千万别学最后那个亮绿顶栏网页，最烦那种带浅灰弥散外阴影的大圆角白卡片了，统统给我切成最硬朗的直角和单像素框线就行

palette.why: 第 1 份是近乎纯黑的单色暗黑模式，与第 2 份的深蓝底加大面积鲜艳半透明彩块、第 3 份的白底加高亮翠绿色有极其显著的色彩关系和明暗差异。

by_label.A: 大标题及特定引言段落使用明显的衬线体（宋体质感），正文使用无衬线黑体，文字排版较紧凑，大量出现类似表格键值对的密集信息排列。
by_label.B: 全无衬线英文字体，特征排版为“极大字号的粗体主标题 + 下方紧贴水平短实线 + 全大写且字间距拉得很宽的小字号副标题”，正文段落行距极为宽松。
by_label.C: 常规的无衬线英文字体，各层级字号对比适中，标题多为常规粗体且常居中对齐，段落文本字距正常，无夸张的大字号或特殊的字间距排版。

typography.why: 第 2 份拥有非常典型的现代英文排版套路（超大粗体+宽字距全大写细字），与第 1 份的中式衬线混排及第 3 份的中规中矩常规无衬线排版一眼即可区分。

by_label.A: 几乎不使用任何框线或卡片容器组件，内容直接漂浮在纯色背景上，纯靠留白和极细的灰色水平单实线来分隔信息层级。
by_label.B: 组件呈现极致的直角硬线条风格，按钮是完全无圆角的纯白线框（透明底），表单输入框是无外发光无描边的暗色直角块。
by_label.C: 大量依赖白色卡片容器承载内容，卡片边缘和内部图片均带有明显的圆角处理，且卡片四周带有柔和的浅灰色外阴影；下拉菜单也呈现为带轻阴影的圆角白框。

component.why: 第 3 份的核心特征是“大面积使用带浅阴影的圆角白卡片”，这与前两份完全扁平、无卡片、全直角的硬朗风格形成了明确的分野，能够作为反面要求下达。

user_prompt_en:
We are putting together the new class schedule booking interface for Two Rivers. Because our catalog is growing rapidly, the information architecture needs to be flawless, allowing users to filter, search, and book sessions without getting lost in a maze of pages. I need a single-page application feel where the state updates dynamically based on user interaction, rather than relying on traditional page reloads. The interface should be split into a persistent navigation column on the left and a dense, highly structured main workspace on the right.

Looking at the screenshots I provided, please take that exact approach to the text sizing and structural hierarchy, though you can adjust the specific font family to match our brand guidelines. I specifically want to replicate how the text weights guide the eye. Notice how the primary page header is the largest and most heavily weighted, while the headers for individual sections within the main area are still bold but noticeably scaled down. That is exactly the structural clarity I need. For the navigation column, use that same tiny, all-caps treatment for the category labels, just like the word 'WORKSPACE' shown in the images. When we get to the actual booking form inputs, follow the images by using standard dark text for the field labels above the boxes, and reserve the lighter grey exclusively for the placeholder text inside the empty inputs so users can instantly distinguish them.

The left column must function as the primary control center. It needs a dedicated search input at the top allowing users to instantly filter the schedule by class name or instructor. Below the search, organize the navigation into distinct groups. Use those tiny caps for group labels like 'PROGRAMS', 'LOCATIONS', and 'SYSTEM'. Under 'PROGRAMS', list interactive filters for our core offerings: Core Dynamics, Restorative Flow, and Advanced Seminars. Clicking any of these should instantly filter the main workspace view.

The main workspace needs to display a complex, stateful weekly schedule. By default, it should show an interactive grid for the current week. Each class block in the grid must display the start time, duration, instructor name, and current capacity status. When a user clicks on a specific class block, I do not want a popup. Instead, the grid should smoothly compress to the left, revealing a detailed booking pane on the right side of the screen. This slide-out pane is where the complexity lies. It must present the full class syllabus, prerequisite information, and the actual booking form.

Because our primary users are often technical staff coordinating group training, include a toggle switch at the top of the schedule view. This toggle should switch the main area from the visual weekly grid into a dense, sortable raw data table. Inside the expanded booking pane, after a user fills out their attendee details and hits the submit button, the state should change to a confirmation view. To cater to our system administrators, this confirmation state should display a stylized code block showing the simulated JSON payload of their booking request alongside the standard human-readable success message. This ensures the interface serves both our standard practitioners and the technical team managing the API integrations. Ensure the transitions between the calendar view, the data table, and the slide-out booking pane are fluid and immediately responsive to user input.

user_prompt_zh:
**概述**：为我们的非营利法律援助项目搭建专业志愿者招募单页。这次面向的是执业律师和心理辅导师，核心诉求是信息获取极度清晰无障碍，让他们一眼看清门槛与排班时间。

**页面结构**：放弃那种常规的流式大块留白，我希望像截图里最后那张粗黑边框的米色页面那样，用紧贴的粗黑线把页面严密划分成大小不一的矩形网格，带点旧报纸排版的紧凑感。拿一处网格做个类似它那样的带时间轴特征的侧栏，用来展示报名和审核的步骤。

**视觉呈现**：文字阅读体验要好。那个青色大标题横幅的单栏文章页上的字就非常好，主标题字号巨大且全用大写字母，无衬线体，正文的行距和字号够大，段落极其分明。但注意，那个带粉色渐变顶栏的图文页里的颜色我绝对不要，粉橙色横断面和浅粉色点缀太花哨了，咱们只要干练稳重的纯白底配黑灰字。另外，带红按钮那个渐变页里的实心深色底块和方块社交图标，还有蓝色托管宣传页里那堆大圆角悬浮阴影卡片和半圆胶囊按钮，这两种形式我们全避开，就要最朴素低调的细实线框按键就行。

**交互状态**：表单区需要做一个平滑的多步骤状态切换，点击左侧专业类别时，右侧的资格证上传和时间选择框能动态平滑切换，不整页跳转。

**验收**：代码装在一个HTML文件里，手机端看时全部网格能顺滑折叠成竖排。

by_label.A: 由顶部横幅、三列等宽网格图文块、以及底部多列深色页脚组合成的传统分块布局。
by_label.B: 以顶部全宽色块为引导，下方居中单列大图和长段落文本为主的流式博客阅读布局。
by_label.C: 交替呈现单图及侧边文本（左右混排）的大区块，辅以大面积留白的稀疏多列文本块。
by_label.D: 顶部使用巨大渐变背景延伸至正文区后方，正文区通过浮动的两列或多列卡片网格交叠在其上。
by_label.E: 摒弃常规流式留白，采用紧贴的粗黑线边框将页面严密划分为多个大小不一的矩形网格（类似表单或报纸排版），包含带时间轴特征的侧边结构。

layout.why: 第 5 份（E）带有极强烈的粗黑实线网格及复古表格排版感，与前四份常规的流式/卡片式网页结构截然不同，极易区分。

by_label.A: 包含大面积深色背景（黑色卡片/深灰页脚），横幅为冷暖交替的模糊渐变色，深红色作为主行动按钮和强调色。
by_label.B: 以纯白底色为主，顶部横幅使用大面积明亮的青色，正文为深灰，辅以少量青色用于小图标。
by_label.C: 以极浅的米白色为主底色，最显著特征是顶部横断面的粉色到粉橙色渐变横幅，文字中也带有浅粉色点缀。
by_label.D: 亮蓝色系为主，大面积明快的天蓝到深蓝色渐变作为底板，内容卡片为纯白色，深色及蓝色系按钮点缀。
by_label.E: 复古卡其色/米黄色作为单一页面底色，除图片外唯一使用的是纯黑色的线条、文字块和小方块，形成强烈的黑黄对比。

palette.why: 反面点名的第 3 份（C）拥有非常醒目且面积巨大的粉色/粉橙色渐变这一独占特征，判分时极易识别成品有没有沾染这种颜色。

by_label.A: 常规无衬线体，标题加粗，正文字号较小且排版较为紧凑，具备多级标题字号对比。
by_label.B: 无衬线体，文章主标题全部使用大写字母且字号巨大，正文为适宜长时间阅读的较大行距和字号，段落层次分明。
by_label.C: 使用极细字重（Light/Thin）的无衬线体，整体视觉极其轻盈，标题也没有明显的加粗处理。
by_label.D: 现代几何感无衬线体，常规的SaaS类产品粗细搭配，各级标题字号平滑递减。
by_label.E: 中文排版为主，字重相对统一，字号偏小，排列紧密规整，段落边缘整齐如印刷品。

typography.why: 第 2 份（B）拥有主标题全大写、正文行距较大等典型的博客排版特征，但全大写的特征如果模型忽略，正文排版可能会与D有几分相似，有轻微混淆风险。

by_label.A: 主按钮为无圆角（或极小圆角）的方形实心色块；内容区块直接铺深色背景底块无边框；社交图标被包裹在带圆角的正方形底板中。
by_label.B: 社交分享区由带有实心颜色的细小圆角方块构成；未见明显的独立内容卡片组件（图片无额外修饰）。
by_label.C: 使用了极细的纯线框（幽灵）按钮，无背景填充；图文块依靠大量留白分隔，无实际的底板或边框组件。
by_label.D: 大量使用具有大圆角的白色浮动卡片（带轻微阴影）；按钮均为非常圆润的半圆形胶囊按钮（如Contact Us / Buy Now）。
by_label.E: 无常规意义上的按钮或浮动卡片，所有组件边界均由粗实不带圆角的黑色直线构成，并使用实心黑色小方块作为列表装饰。

component.why: 点名的两份特征不仅明确而且截然相反：第 1 份是硬朗方正无阴影的色块按钮和卡片，第 4 份是极端圆润且带有悬浮阴影的大圆角卡片与胶囊按钮，彼此绝不会混淆。

user_prompt_en:
I am putting together a real-time air quality monitoring interface for a regional public health initiative. As a data analyst, I need the environmental metrics to be absolutely front and center, highly accurate, and easy to parse without forcing users to dig through endless navigation menus. The core of this project is a live, interactive geographic visualization of AQI, PM2.5, sulfur dioxide, and other critical pollutant levels. We are primarily building this utility for a middle-aged and older demographic who check these metrics daily before their morning exercises, so readability and clear numerical presentation are my absolute top priorities. I still want the whole experience to feel advanced and technologically forward, like a modern smart-city command center, but it must remain accessible. I have a very specific requirement for the type: I want all the body text and data labels to use a classic serif face with elegant thin-thick stroke contrasts. It provides a level of traditional readability that our older users appreciate and trust, while looking surprisingly sharp and authoritative on modern high-resolution displays.

For the actual structure of the interface, I was looking at that full-screen graphing tool you can see in the final set of images. I really like how that is blocked out, and I want to take the exact same approach here. The entire browser viewport should just be the interactive map acting as our main grid. Please do not box it in with margins or heavy headers. Instead of a math legend, we will have our AQI color scale and summary metrics floating as a distinct block in the top left corner of the map. Then, down at the bottom of the screen, I want a fixed, docked control panel that spans the width of the window, just like the slider console in that graph example. This bottom area will house our complex interactions: an interactive time-scrubber to watch historical pollution clouds moving across the region, and multi-select toggles for switching between the different pollutant data layers.

To make this highly legible, I want to pull the colors directly from that first set of screenshots with the conference speaker schedules. Give me that exact pure white base for the main interface panels and cards, and use that deep purple-blue photographic tone for the underlying base map styling or empty states. For any interactive elements, warning thresholds on the map, or active filter toggles in the bottom console, use that striking bright orange. It highlights exactly what the user needs to see immediately. Now, for the physical shapes of these panels and controls, I actually want you to look at the dark media platform in the middle screenshots. I want our floating legend and the bottom console to use those exact small block treatments. Give them those very pronounced rounded corners and subtle bright borders. The filtering buttons in our bottom control panel should be those large, highly rounded capsule shapes, maybe using semi-transparent dark backgrounds for inactive states and solid bright colors for active ones, exactly as seen on those media cards.

Even though we are building a high-tech map with rounded floating elements, I want the atmosphere of the site to carry the exact feeling of that white and orange event page. It should not feel like a casual media app or an academic research tool; it needs to project that formal, practical, and highly active business environment. It should feel like a serious, pragmatic public utility where the numbers are authoritative and ready to be acted upon. As users interact with the time slider in the bottom console, the map should smoothly animate the pollution heatmaps transitioning over time, keeping the stateful views fluid. The data needs to feel alive but grounded in absolute precision, with clear numerical tooltips popping up instantly as you hover over different city districts on the map.

by_label.D: 流行的现代组件风格，按钮为完全两端半圆的纯色胶囊形状（绿色），特色图标由深色极细线框图形叠加在稍稍错位的浅绿色实心圆底上构成。

user_prompt_en:
**Project Overview**
This document outlines the requirements for a new, highly accessible note-taking and archiving interface designed specifically for our community outreach volunteers and neighborhood organizers. Our teams are often on the ground in chaotic town hall environments or community centers, needing a reliable, distraction-free space to record resident concerns, track mutual aid requests, and draft meeting minutes. Because we operate on a shoestring budget and rely on volunteers ranging from high school students to retirees, this tool must be exceptionally clear, lightweight, and immediately understandable without any training manual. The primary focus is on a single-page application that elegantly combines an active drafting area with a structured, visually distinct archive of previous records. We cannot afford complex onboarding, so the mechanics must feel natural from the first click.

**Workspace Structure**
The entire application should exist on a single, unified screen to prevent our users from getting lost in nested menus or losing their place during a fast-paced meeting. I was looking at that dark page with all the digital art pieces, and I want our main workspace blocked out exactly like that. Start with a prominent, large, centered header area at the very top—though instead of an exploration prompt, we will use this space for our active, expanding text editor where the live note-taking actually happens. Directly beneath this active editor area, I need a full-width section that displays our saved notes, arranged just like the content on that dark page: a strict, four-column equal-width grid of individual cards. First, present a single horizontal row of exactly four cards dedicated exclusively to "Pinned Neighborhood Action Plans." Below that row, flow the rest of the standard meeting notes into a multi-row grid, continuing that exact same four-column blocking downward as more notes are added.

**Interface Aesthetics**
Visual clarity is non-negotiable for our volunteers, many of whom have astigmatism or vision sensitivities. I need you to pull the exact colors from that light page showing the side-by-side version comparisons. Use that extensive, clean white and very pale grey for the entire background and the individual note cards to keep the environment feeling open, calm, and uncluttered. For any primary actions—like the 'Save Note' button, the active cursor, tag indicators, and essential system icons—grab that high-visibility, bright blue-purple they are using there. It provides fantastic contrast and directs the eye without feeling aggressive or corporate.

Crucially, I have already decided on the text sizing for readability, and this is an absolute rule: all body text across the entire interface must be 18px or larger. I want this enforced everywhere, full stop. Anything smaller than that, my mother cannot read, and neither can half of our senior committee members. If it feels too big or clunky to you, adjust the padding inside the cards or the editor margins to compensate, but under no circumstances should you shrink the actual text size.

**Editor Mechanics & Data**
The top centered section (our active editor) must be a robust, stateful text area. It should support rich text seamlessly but quietly. When a user clicks into it, the input area should smoothly expand downward to accommodate long-form typing, gently pushing the four-column grid below it further down the page without jarring jumps. Provide a minimalist formatting toolbar that only appears when text is highlighted by the user (a floating tooltip style), offering just bold, bulleted lists, and a yellow highlight option. We do not want a permanent, cluttered ribbon toolbar that distracts from the content.

Each active note needs clearly labeled input fields for "Resident Name," "Neighborhood Block," and "Topic Tags" directly above the main text body. The wording should be conversational and encouraging, like "What did the neighborhood discuss today?" rather than sterile system prompts like "Input Text Here."

**State Management & Interactivity**
Since Wi-Fi connections in community centers are notoriously unreliable, the editor must manage state locally with high resilience. Implement a silent autosave feature that captures keystroke changes every five seconds, displaying a subtle, unobtrusive "Saved locally" checkmark near the title, utilizing that blue-purple accent color.

When a user finishes a meeting note and clicks a prominent "Archive to Board" button, the active editor should clear itself with a gentle fade animation. Simultaneously, the newly created note must instantly slide into the top-left position of the four-column grid below, smoothly shifting the older note cards one spot to the right to make room.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- The active editing area expands dynamically based on content length without breaking the page width or overlapping the grid section.
- All background and card surfaces utilize the bright white and light grey from the comparison page, with interactive elements strictly using the designated blue-purple accent color.
- The saved notes section rigidly follows the four-column card arrangement derived from the dark artwork page, maintaining top alignment even when individual note titles vary in length.
- An automated test confirms that absolutely no body text renders below 18px under any viewport condition.
- The local autosave successfully retains text in the editor even if the browser tab is accidentally refreshed or closed.
- Keyboard navigation fully supports tabbing through the editor inputs, formatting options, and all cards in the lower grid, ensuring total accessibility for volunteers relying on screen readers.

user_prompt_en:
**Overview**
This document defines the requirements for our new Enterprise Subscription Configurator. Currently, our enterprise procurement buyers face a high friction point: they have to contact sales just to get a baseline estimate for their customized infrastructure needs. This page will serve as a self-serve, highly interactive pricing builder that allows technical leads and procurement officers to dial in their exact requirements and instantly visualize their projected annual costs and ROI. The goal is transparency, precision, and accelerating the enterprise sales cycle.

**Core Business Logic & Data Requirements**
The configurator must calculate costs based on three main variable axes. Please embed these exact parameters into the application logic:
1. Base Platform SLA: The starting tier is the "Standard SLA" at $2,000/month. The user can toggle to "Mission Critical 99.99% SLA" which shifts the base to $5,500/month.
2. Provisioned Compute Nodes: Users will adjust this via a slider (Range: 10 to 1,000 nodes). The pricing is tiered: nodes 10-100 are $45 each; nodes 101-500 are $35 each; nodes 501+ are $25 each.
3. Dedicated Support Add-ons: A series of toggle switches for "Technical Account Manager" (adds $1,500/mo flat) and "On-Premise Deployment Sync" (adds 15% to the total calculated cost).

The application must maintain these states seamlessly and update the final "Estimated Monthly Commitment" and "Annual Projection" figures in real-time without ever reloading the page.

**Page Structure & Stateful Views**
Instead of a long scrolling page, the entire experience must be contained within a single centralized interactive unit. 
- **Header Area**: A central, precise vector graphic serving as an anchor, surrounded by the primary title: "ENTERPRISE INFRASTRUCTURE DEPLOYMENT".
- **Configuration Panel**: Below the header, present the inputs. First, the slider for Compute Nodes, styled cleanly with the current selected value displayed above the thumb. Below that, arrange the toggle switches for the Add-ons. 
- **Visualization & Quote Area**: At the bottom of the active area, render a dynamic SVG-based data visualization—a simple line chart or bar graph that animates to show the cost efficiency as node volume increases. Below the chart, display the final calculated price in a large, clear format with a primary "Request Formal Quote" button.

**Look and Feel**
For the visual execution, we are strictly adopting the design language you can see in the attached screenshots. The entire configurator must sit inside that exact same massive, pure white container with the prominent rounded corners and the very subtle, soft outer shadow. Keep the background identical to what is shown—that faint, dotted, light-greyish canvas that gives it a highly technical, blueprint-like feel. 

I want to retain the exact color strategy and text hierarchy from the reference. Use that deep purple for centered subheadings (like our configuration section titles) and the precise magenta for uppercase circular or accent text. The descriptive body text should remain that clean, legible dark grey. We need to preserve the overarching vibe of the screenshots: extremely spacious, clean, and restrained. Do not clutter the card; let the generous whitespace communicate a premium, precise enterprise product. 

For the top anchor graphic, design a custom abstract vector representing "Cloud Infrastructure" (rather than the pen nib shown), but borrow the specific interaction tricks from the frames. When the user hovers over this central graphic, it should reveal a crisp white arrow icon inside it, just like the second image demonstrates. Furthermore, ensure that if a user highlights any text on the page to copy it (like the pricing breakdown), the text selection background uses that exact deep blue color captured in the second screenshot.

**Interaction & Motion**
The transitions within this card must be flawless. 
- When a user adjusts the Compute Node slider, the numeric values must tick up smoothly, and the SVG data visualization should animate its path to reflect the new cost curve dynamically. 
- Toggling the Add-ons should trigger a subtle color shift in the toggle component itself, and the final total at the bottom should counter-animate (rolling numbers) to the new price.
- Hovering over the "Request Formal Quote" button should provide a distinct but professional feedback state, gently raising the shadow rather than doing anything overly flashy.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- The page must be delivered as a single, self-contained HTML file including all CSS, JS, and inline SVGs. 
- The tiered pricing logic must be mathematically flawless; testing exactly 150 nodes with Mission Critical SLA and a TAM must yield the correct exact dollar amount instantly.
- The entire application must fit gracefully within the single centered white card layout without overflowing or requiring page-level scroll on standard 1080p desktop monitors.
- All custom hover states (including the white arrow graphic reveal) and the specific blue text selection highlight must be implemented precisely as described.
- The layout must remain responsive; on mobile viewports, the large central card should gracefully adapt its padding and font sizes while retaining its distinct rounded-corner container.

user_prompt_en: We are crafting the creative narrative for a next-generation resume builder, and I want the interface to feel like an immersive, focused workspace rather than a standard web form. I want the whole page on a dark ground with light text on it, creating a quiet theater for the user's career story. The spatial organization needs to be incredibly tight. Looking at the final set of screenshots with those massive flat color tiles, I want you to structure our page exactly like that. We should have a wide, edge-to-edge overview bar running right across the top to show completion progress, and then the entire canvas below that should be seamlessly paved with interlocking, different-sized rectangular blocks. One large block for the live preview, a tall column for work experience, and smaller tight rectangles for skills and contact details, all fitting together without any loose empty space between them. It has to be strictly responsive, adapting gracefully so the proportions remain stunning whether the user is on a massive studio monitor or tweaking their CV on a phone. When it comes to the actual words inside these builder sections, I am drawn to how the text is handled in that dark settings panel with the starry background. Bring in that exact text treatment: I love the pairing of the regular-weight, crisp main titles sitting directly above the noticeably smaller, dimmed-out supplementary descriptions, and please include those tiny, colorful micro-tags sitting next to the titles for things like new feature callouts. It gives everything a highly editorial, precise rhythm. However, keep the interactive elements completely grounded. Looking at the very first few shots with the web map, that is exactly what I do not want—do not make our buttons or input fields look like those heavily shadowed, glossy 3D spheres with the retro vertical gradients. I want our interactive areas to be sharply defined by simple, ultra-thin flat lines, completely stripped of any volume or shine, so the focus stays entirely on the words being typed.

user_prompt_zh: 搞个拉新的开发者API文档单页啊，首屏转化冲击力要拉满，这块就瞄准那个白底有错落大图组合的学校网页来，左边上巨大号的抓手文案，右侧搞三张错开拼贴的真实业务调用截图，下面紧贴一行极具说服力的高频转化数字比如千万级QPS之类的，进到核心文档区就是大量长正文了因为主要就是限制在iPad横屏上用所以沉浸阅读体验要做到极致，侧边得加那种锚点导航滚过去还能带高亮跟踪的钩子功能，文字阅读感上我觉得那个带手写签名的博客网页里透出的感觉特别好，那种松散透气的字间距还有细灰斜体字块特别适合拿来做API报错说明或者技术引言，至于配色千万别搞得像那个黑底亮橙色按钮卖车的页面或者那个一会浅灰粉蓝一会深黑的页面那样，颜色太晃眼不够B端，我就要最克制的高级科技蓝配纯白就行，还有个事就是那个底色像奶油一样而且图片文字全没边框没阴影糊在一起的页面那种风格我也真受不了，完全没有点击转化欲望，咱们的接口参数面板和CTA按钮必须得有实实在在的悬浮微投影和清楚的细描边，最后页面里再加个代码块一键复制的状态切换动画方便熬夜打码的兄弟们无脑接入就算完事了

user_prompt_zh:
我们准备给大学历史学院做一个全新的主页，因为下周就要在主楼中庭的超大屏幕上投屏展示，所以整体框架要大气，远距离看文字和区块也能有足够的张力。整个网站的氛围必须是沉静深邃、幽暗内敛的，要散发一种极强的历史厚重感和叙事绘本的味道，就像那个讲大禹治水故事的网页给人的触动一样。颜色方面正好从那个治水的页面里取，大面积铺满那种深灰蓝和深泥土色，文字用纯白色，这样在暗底上的对比度在大屏上才立得住。

版式结构上，我觉得最开始那个宠物洗护预约网站的做法就很对味，首屏采用非对称的左右分栏，左侧放具有强烈视觉引导的大号文字，右侧悬浮一个快捷指引卡片，往下滚动后则自然过渡到三列平齐的信息卡片排列。为了撑起学院的学术感，文字字体的选择可以参考最后那个带紫色渐变的手机软件页面，大标题统统用那种粗重且具有现代感的衬线字体，字号要给足，正文则搭配常规的无衬线字体，形成强烈的混搭对比。至于页面里具体的按钮、输入框和卡片，千万别搞成那个带侧边栏的博客网页里那种全白底色、薄荷绿药丸标签和全圆角按钮，也绝对不要像那个蓝灰相间的旧排版网页里那种深色微小又没边框的死板矩形链接。我想要的是线条极其锋利、带有微透明磨砂质感的锐角几何容器。

页面内容顺下来大概分这么几块：起手是刚才说的分栏大导语；往下紧接一个横向滚动的交互式大事记时间轴，因为这里的历史档案条目非常庞大，必须做成带视差动效的水平滑动，并且带有平滑的年代筛选功能以免拖得太长；接着是三个核心研究方向的图文介绍；然后是一个专门用来展示优秀毕业生去向和校友评价的轮播图，作为吸引新生报考的钩子；最后是联络表单和招生指引。新闻文献库那块也要注意，信息密度极高，一定要做好无感分页处理。

by_label.A: 首屏采用非对称的左右分栏，左侧为大号文字，右侧悬浮表单卡片；下方转为三列平齐的信息卡片排列。
by_label.B: 包含顶部导航和横向的标签云，主体内容分为左侧的两列图文卡片网格和右侧的个人/搜索侧边栏。
by_label.C: 主体内容在一个居中定宽的容器内，划分为两列或三列紧凑的纯文本与链接区块排列。
by_label.D: 使用全屏铺满的背景插画，没有传统的栏目或网格划分，文字内容自由悬浮在画面左上角。
by_label.E: 典型的单列落地页结构，首屏左文右图（手机模型），向下滚动则有居中对齐的大段文字和带图标的双列特征介绍。

layout.why: 第1份独有的左侧超大标题配合右侧表单卡片的非对称首屏布局，与其余各份的标准博客网格、多列文本或全屏插画截然不同。

by_label.A: 大面积使用暖米色作为底色，文字为极深的颜色，按钮和点缀色使用深墨绿色。
by_label.B: 以纯白色为绝对主底色，文字为深灰色，主色和强调色为极其鲜艳的薄荷绿。
by_label.C: 顶部横幅为青蓝色，主体背景为微微偏灰绿的米色，链接和按钮色保持与顶部一致的青蓝色。
by_label.D: 整体呈现暗色调的阴雨氛围，以大面积的深灰蓝、深泥土色为主，文字使用白色以保证在暗底上的对比度。
by_label.E: 大面积留白，搭配纯黑色的高对比文字，最显眼的是贯穿页面的高饱和蓝紫色渐变色块。

palette.why: 第4份是5组参考中唯一采用深暗色系（深蓝灰）作为主背景的页面，在明暗倾向上与其他四份明亮底色的页面形成绝对反差。

by_label.A: 极其粗大、具有几何感的无衬线字体被用于各级大标题，与正常字号的正文形成了极其夸张的字号反差。
by_label.B: 全局使用常规的无衬线字体，标题字重较轻，各层级字号差异适中，整体阅读感平缓。
by_label.C: 使用较为纤细常规的无衬线体，字号普遍偏小，即使是标题也没有拉开很大的字号差距。
by_label.D: 标题和正文统一使用古典的衬线字体，字号偏小，字重较轻，透出强烈的叙事和书卷气息。
by_label.E: 大标题使用粗重且具有现代感的衬线字体（字号很大），而正文则搭配常规的无衬线字体，形成字族上的混搭对比。

typography.why: 第5份在大号标题上使用了引人注目的粗衬线体，而正文搭配无衬线体，这种特定组合与第1份的纯巨型无衬线、第4份的纯古典衬线都有显著区别。

user_prompt_en:
**Overview**
This document outlines the comprehensive requirements for our new B2B fresh grocery ordering portal. Our primary target users are busy restaurant managers, executive chefs, and catering directors who need to restock daily produce rapidly, often at the end of a gruelling shift. The core product value here is relentless efficiency and order accuracy. We are dealing with bulk quantities, constantly fluctuating daily market prices, and strict delivery cut-offs. Similar to how Amazon's frictionless one-click ordering philosophy completely removes psychological barriers to purchase, we need this portal to get out of the user's way. A chef should be able to log in, locate their usual items, compile a 50-item procurement list, and confirm the delivery in under three minutes. The final engineering deliverable must be a single-file HTML solution, heavily relying on tables and numbers, so our field sales representatives can demonstrate the platform offline instantly on their laptops during client site visits.

**Page structure**
Let's organize the page's structural footprint to be similar to the village house renovation site you see in the last few shots. We want a massive, edge-to-edge full-width hero image right at the top. This prime real estate will feature our seasonal fresh produce or a farm-to-table promotional banner to set the correct business context immediately upon loading. Directly below that hero section, drop the main content area into an asymmetrical two-column grid. The wider left column will serve as the main workhorse of the application, housing the core product categories (e.g., Organic Leafy Greens, Root Vegetables, Citrus & Exotics) and the actual tabular ordering interfaces. The narrower right column will hold a persistent, sticky order summary and checkout action area, ensuring the running financial total and item count are always in the user's peripheral vision as they scroll deeply down the inventory lists.

**Visual**
Because our users often place these orders late at night in dimly lit back-office environments, we are going with a strictly dark mode approach. Grab the specific colors from that 3D geometry dashboard page. Use that deep blue-grey or teal-tinted dark background across the entire application viewport, set the main reading text to crisp white or light grey, and utilize those striking bright turquoise or cyan highlights to immediately draw the eye to interactive elements, active states, and critical inventory numbers.

For the text treatments, borrow the approach from the light server request heatmap page. Everything should utilize a clean, legible sans-serif. Stick to lighter font weights and maintain a medium visual contrast so it remains exceptionally easy on the eyes during marathon ordering sessions. Since this UI relies so heavily on dense data tables (SKUs, weights, price per kg, pallet configurations), do exactly what that heatmap does around its grid: use densely packed, very small text for all the unit labels, origin metadata, and secondary identifiers.

When you build out the actionable items and lists, look back at the village project site again. We need those straightforward, solid buttons with sharp right angles or just the absolute slightest hint of a rounded corner. For our extensive product lists, construct them like the ultra-minimal data tables shown on that specific page—absolutely no heavy outer borders, utilizing only thin, subtle horizontal grey lines to separate the individual rows.

**Interaction**
The primary functional hook driving this prototype is the shopping cart logic. We need a working frontend-only cart pre-loaded with a few dummy items (like 5kg crates of Roma tomatoes or 10kg sacks of yellow onions) so internal stakeholders can test the interaction loop immediately. When a user clicks a button to add a new case, or tweaks a numeric input field to increase an order to 15kg, the running financial total and the line-item count in the right-hand summary column must update instantly without requiring a full page refresh. Even though the data presentation is extremely dense, the interface must remain highly responsive. On tablet or narrow mobile device widths, the right-hand summary column should fold neatly beneath the main catalog, or potentially dock rigidly to the bottom of the screen as a sticky action banner.

**Acceptance**
- The provided HTML file must be fully self-contained, with all CSS styling and JavaScript logic embedded directly within the document, functioning perfectly on a machine with no internet connection.
- A strict CSS print media query stylesheet is mandatory. If a user hits Cmd+P to print their final order manifest to stick on the kitchen wall, the page must format cleanly onto standard A4 paper without any grid elements overlapping, clipping, or breaking awkwardly across pages.
- The shopping cart script must correctly calculate individual row totals (input quantity multiplied by the fixed unit price) and accurately aggregate a grand total at the bottom of the narrow right column, utilizing the provided fake data arrays.
- At a standard 1280px desktop resolution, there must be absolutely no horizontal scrolling required to view the full product tables, the input fields, or the summary panel.

tags.内容体量: 以表格和数字为主

user_prompt_zh: 想给写字的朋友们弄个海报编辑器界面，日常做图用。界面信息密度得高，结构就看那个带网格卡片的工具包页，顶上留宽大头图做预览，往下接横排三列的栏目，核心区是左边文本导航配右边多列网格卡片放模板。我习惯暗色，颜色希望像那个深棕色动物游戏界面，极暗深棕底配亮橙色按钮，字用浅黄色。侧边参数多，字的感觉照着白底分栏电商结账页来，整体字号偏小，完全服务于表单功能，靠适度的加粗和灰色区分标签，别搞巨大的标题。控件要利落，像带深色顶栏的落地页里那样，按钮全是无圆角阴影的直角扁平纯色块，列表带纯色小勾，指示器用细线空心圆套实心点就行。

by_label.A: 顶部通栏导航叠加在大图上，下方内容区呈左文本列表右图片的简单的两栏并排
by_label.B: 内容集中在屏幕中央，采用多行多列的固定网格排列方形图标，四周留出大面积空白
by_label.C: 顶部为极简的居中导航，主体区域是左侧较宽的堆叠表单与右侧较窄的订单卡片构成的不对称两栏结构
by_label.D: 包含全宽大头图，向下过渡到横排三列的数字指标栏，再向下为左侧文本导航+右侧多列瀑布流式的卡片网格布局，信息密度最高

layout.why: 第 4 份具备独有的横向三列数字栏和多列大量组件卡片组成的网格区域，与其他页面的布局结构完全不同

by_label.A: 灰白色背景，顶部深黑灰导航条，主导强调色为明亮的天蓝色（用于按钮和文字链接）
by_label.B: 极暗的深棕色纯色背景，大量使用亮橙色作为强对比的强调色（主按钮和高亮边框），文字偏浅黄/白色
by_label.C: 大面积纯白背景，局部辅以浅灰底色（订单项），强调色为低饱和的红棕色（用于主按钮）
by_label.D: 纯白背景，头图部分带有自然风景色，强调色为醒目的玫粉色（用于按钮和小标签），大标题为深黑色

palette.why: 第 2 份是四张图中唯一采用深色暗黑系背景（深棕色）的，与另外三份大面积浅色背景形成决定性反差

by_label.A: 首屏中心有一个字号极大的粗体标题，正文相对细小且颜色较浅，字号层级落差非常剧烈
by_label.B: 标题使用了带有活泼/粗体感的中文字体，带有轻微的发光或阴影效果，底部操作提示字号极小
by_label.C: 排版完全服务于表单功能，缺乏巨大的展示型标题，整体字号偏小，利用适度的加粗和灰色系区分表单标签与正文
by_label.D: 主标题采用极粗的无衬线黑体，三列数字指标字号特大，正文颜色偏浅，大粗体小浅字对比极为强烈

typography.why: 第 3 份是典型的表单实用排版，字号整体偏小，完全没有A和D那种用于视觉冲击的巨型大标题，特征能够辨别

by_label.A: 按钮为完全直角的扁平纯色块，没有任何圆角和阴影；轮播指示器由细线空心圆环和实心圆点组成；列表带纯色小勾图标
by_label.B: 选中项表现为带有橙色发光效果和边框的微圆角方形卡片，主操作按钮为大圆角胶囊状
by_label.C: 输入框为带有极细浅灰边框的微圆角矩形，包含全实心的微圆角按钮，右侧的摘要区被一个细线灰框包裹
by_label.D: 大量使用带有弥散投影效果的大圆角卡片，以及带有彩色实心底色的圆角小标签/徽章

component.why: 第 1 份的按钮采用了锋利的直角（零圆角）且完全扁平无边框，这与C的细线微圆角表单和D的大圆角带阴影卡片有明显差异

user_prompt_zh:
我这边马上要给客户交一版AI智能写作助手的发布落地页，需要你帮我写一份单文件形式的代码，交付标准得高一点，代码结构必须干净，方便他们接手后自己改文案。这是个多板块的推广页，需要带有顶部导航、中间的互动表单，且移动端的响应式适配必须做好。

页面开头首屏我想参考那个带有雕像照片的浅白主页，左边放我们产品的核心价值文案，比如写上“一秒生成懂你的工作报告”，右边配一个产品界面的操作大图，这种左文右图的不对称结构看着挺有张力的。顺着往下划是核心特色功能区，这里我觉得可以直接参考刚才那个主页中下段展示人员的做法，做成一排四个没有边框的图文块垂直排开，客户就喜欢这种不拖泥带水的设计。

文字这块咱们抓一下视觉重点，就像最后面那个画着黑色手机的蓝白工具网页那样，页面里各个级别的标题一定要全部用无衬线体并且加上很重的加粗，跟下面稍微偏淡偏细的正文拉开极为显著的粗细对比。标题要重，正文要轻，这样客户的老板看的时候一眼就能扫到核心买点，不会觉得一堆文字挤在一起没层次。

中间应用场景展示的部分，咱们要做成一个个带演示图的方块。这里的细节你看一下那个放了一堆开会和握手照片的橙色列表页，我们要那种带有极浅色细边框的高度完整的卡片。最关键的是要在卡片图片上面悬浮一个小方块，用来标明这篇是“周报”还是“公文”，就像它那个图片上悬浮的橙色日期一样，然后在卡片最底部也加上一条细细的横向分割线，底下放点类似生成字数或者使用人次的信息栏。

至于颜色的事情，我得特别嘱咐一句，千万别搞成那个带红色山脉背景页面的样子，那种浓重的暗红渐变铺底，加上一块块死黑的内容区，还有大红大绿那么扎眼的高饱和度警示条，实在是不适合咱们这次要推的现代效率工具。我的想法是咱们就要干干净净的纯白底色，局部按钮或者显眼的地方点缀一点亮蓝色就行，看着通透、现代一点，完全不需要那种压抑沉重的东西。

最后页面底部需要一个让用户留邮箱申请内测的区域，简单干脆点，写一句“立刻开启智能创作”，下面放个大点的输入框配个主色调的提交按钮就行。页面的导航栏滑下去的时候记得做个吸顶效果，移动端下要把导航折叠成常见的汉堡菜单形式，之前我给他们做别的项目没加上这个被念叨了半天。

recipe.persona_desc: 自由设计师给客户交付

user_prompt_zh: 最近在筹备社区的习惯打卡小工具就是带大家一起每天打卡喝水看书啥的，想弄个让老人家用着方便清楚的网页，上面得有个表单让大家自己加习惯，也得有个导航能切着看。我看图里那张排版像古文书的挺好，那个很有传统气息的中文衬线字，从右往左竖排偶尔又横竖混着排的感觉，字号主次分得清，咱们的文字也要这种感觉。记进度的部分做成那个测血压心跳界面里的样子，就用那种有圆角和浅浅阴影的白卡片包起来，里面的进度像它那样放点环形刻度条和小折线图，状态也用那种胶囊一样的标签标出来。整体排布千万别学那个全是暗暗的风景照网格，全屏一点边距没留看着头晕，也别像顶上绿色一大片那个商业页搞个巨大花哨的彩色通栏下面又空落落的，普普通通按块分好留够边距防误触就行。最关键的整页底色我要深的，字浮在深底上，大晚上打卡不伤眼，记得要在手机屏幕上好用啊

palette.say_zh: 整页底色我要深的，字浮在深底上
palette.say_en: I want the whole page on a dark ground with light text on it
palette.check: 渲染页正文区域的中位明度 V < 0.35
palette.probe: 深色底|深底|暗底|黑底|(?:底色|背景|整页|全页)[^，。、；\n]{0,10}(?:深|暗|黑)|dark[\s-]?(?:ground|background|bg|theme|mode|base|canvas|surface|palette|page)|(?:background|ground|page|canvas|base)[^.!?;\n]{0,24}\bdark\b

by_label.A: 使用了带有传统古籍气质的中文衬线体，大量采用从右至左的竖向排版，部分信息横竖混排。
by_label.B: 使用现代无衬线体，常规横排，数据指标数字（如77 bpm）使用较大字号和加粗处理以作强调。
by_label.C: 几乎无大段文本，仅在每张图片左下角使用了字号极小的全大写无衬线体作为标注。
by_label.D: 使用现代无衬线体，横向排版，标题粗大饱满，正文字重较轻，层级对比十分强烈。

typography.why: 第 1 份极为特殊的竖向排版方式和古典衬线体气质，与其余三份的现代常规横排版形成了降维级别的差异，绝不会认错。

by_label.A: 没有常见的网页表单或按钮控件，主要使用极细的线条和简单的几何方框作为内容分隔标识。
by_label.B: 主要由带有明显圆角和轻微弥散浅阴影的白色卡片构成，包含环形刻度进度条、折线图等数据可视化组件以及胶囊状状态标签。
by_label.C: 没有任何常规意义上的UI组件（如卡片、按钮、输入框），整个页面仅由图片区块无缝拼接而成。
by_label.D: 没有使用带边框或阴影的封闭卡片容器，包含带有微小圆角的实色填充按钮（深色或亮绿色），以及带有3D光影质感的大图标。

component.why: 第 2 份具有典型的医疗数据仪表盘特有组件（环形表盘、阴影数据卡片），这在完全是图片或纯排版的其他参考中是独一份的。

by_label.A: 没有严格的网格或满宽区块，主要依靠大面积的留白和文字排版方向的变换来划分松散的信息层级。
by_label.B: 非全屏流式布局，内容集中在页面中央，以多个不同尺寸的数据卡片组合成悬浮在浅色背景上的仪表盘模块。

user_prompt_en:
**Overview**
The new Midnight Syndicate album, *Void Walker*, drops next month. This landing page is our central hub for the entire digital release. It needs to capture the cinematic, isolationist narrative of the record—think of a late-night drive through an empty, rain-slicked metropolis. We are building a multi-section narrative journey: we need to hype the release, let the fans sample the tracks, sell the upcoming tour tickets, and capture emails for the street team.

**Page structure**
We are pacing this as a cinematic long scroll. Take the structural skeleton from that green marketing page I have open. I want that exact pacing: open with an aggressive, full-width hero block that commands the entire first viewport to set the mood. As the fan scrolls down, shift into an alternating left-and-right flow—put the album art on the left and the liner notes on the right, then swap them for the next track. Further down for the tour dates, drop into that clean, horizontal three-column grid format they used for their stats. We also need a persistent sticky top nav to jump between these beats.

**Visual**
This is a midnight record, so the atmosphere has to be heavy and oppressive. Grab the colors straight out of that dark dashboard screenshot. Submerge the entire background in that deep, inky purple-blue. Against that dark abyss, I want the interactive elements, call-to-actions, and key text to punch through in those high-voltage neon cyans, pinks, and yellows you see on their charts.

Now, for the typography: I've already made the call that all body text must be 18px or larger across the board. Fans shouldn't have to squint to read the lyrics or the venue policies on their phones.

For the tactile interface elements—the audio player containers and the newsletter signup box—look at that white page with the burgers. I love how delicate those containers feel. Wrap our UI in those exact crisp white, sharp-cornered square cards, featuring just that 1px thin mint-green stroke and that incredibly faint drop shadow. It will create a killer, unexpected contrast against our dark void background.

**Interaction**
The top navigation must smoothly anchor-scroll to the respective sections. The track preview section needs custom HTML5 audio controls—when a track is actively playing, the play button should glow with one of our neon highlight colors. The email signup form needs an inline success state showing a thank-you message without bouncing the user to a new page.

**Acceptance**
The entire experience must be delivered as a single, self-contained HTML file.
The alternating desktop flow must gracefully stack into a single vertical column on mobile devices below the 768px breakpoint.
The sticky top nav must shrink in height upon scrolling past the hero section to maximize the viewport space for the content.

user_prompt_zh:
**概述**
我平时写专栏最看重正文排版和长文阅读的沉浸感，但这次帮朋友弄一个商业地产的招商引导页，面对的都是年轻的创意团队，普通的图文堆砌太闷了。我想做一个让人眼前一亮的单页，既能承载大量的园区介绍和招商细则，又能让浏览过程像探险一样有趣。最终目标是留住访客，让他们主动去点开各个地块了解，最后顺畅地提交入驻意向。

**页面结构**
整个页面的框架得跳出传统网页的常规切分。那个全屏绿地游戏界面的Demo网页给了我很大启发，咱们这版也直接以全屏的场景画布（比如手绘的园区俯视图）作为最底层来铺开。
具体区块这么安排：
1. 概览数据区：把项目总面积、可租工位等核心指标，做成固定悬浮在左上角的半透明状态面板。
2. 详细地块介绍：主推重度图文阅读，点击特定区域后触发。
3. 快速动态与联络：在底部居中偶尔弹出的对话框里，放滚动播报的最新签约动态，或者表单入口。

**视觉**
整个网页要营造出一种轻松活泼、复古怀旧的早期 RPG 像素游戏沉浸感，让找办公场地的老板们进来能彻底放松下来。

不过有一点必须避开，背景和主体颜色千万别搞成那个讲兰花温室的米黄色多表格文档页那样。那种全局浅卡其色配深灰文字、再加上棕褐色作为点缀的思路，看着太像满是灰尘的旧档案了，毫无商业园区的活力。我宁愿要深邃一点的暗夜蓝打底，配上高亮度的霓虹色系来提神。

在处理园区介绍那些长正文时，我很喜欢那个带多色服务卡片的个人页里的文字处理手法。大标题直接上极大字号、粗字重的无衬线字体，和正文拉开极其强烈的字号对比。正文的行距一定要放得很宽松，里面如果有园区主理人的寄语，就做成它左侧带粗线描边的引言段落那种感觉，阅读体验绝对好。

至于零碎的小元素，直接去取经第一组那个全屏绿地界面的做法。给我做成深灰色半透明带圆角的悬浮数据面板；里面的招商进度条就弄成那种红绿撞色、粗长条且完全没有外框描边的样式；地块上的标牌或小提示，用跟随式的、带描边的胶囊形状和半透明对话气泡来呈现。

**交互**
底层画布支持拖拽平移，鼠标悬停在不同商业地块上有轻微的浮动反馈。点击底部的气泡可以直接唤起入驻申请表单，表单要能在手机端无缝铺满屏幕。

**验收**
移动端下，左上角的悬浮面板必须能自动折叠成精简状态，绝对不能遮挡画布中心的点击区域。当长文展示层弹出时，底层的游戏感画布要彻底暂停一切动静，确保文字阅读时的绝对专注。

user_prompt_zh:
**概述**：本期重点打造一个全市能源消耗仪表盘。核心诉求是让市政管理人员能一眼看清单日的水电能耗大盘，支持快速下钻查阅异常节点，同时提供一个面向前线的填报入口。系统需要具备多板块视图，且必须适配移动端，以便外勤巡查时随时调阅。

**页面结构**：
1. 左侧全局导航区：用于在不同行政区划或专属重点园区之间快速切换。
2. 顶部概览数据带：展示今日实时总耗电量、耗水量及峰值预警指标，一句话带过涨跌幅走势。
3. 核心趋势图表区：按24小时排布的多列折线图与柱状图，对比历史均值。
4. 异常上报表单模块：包含几个基础的输入框和下拉菜单，供巡检员手动登记离网发电机的燃油消耗。
5. 实时告警信息流：右下角的滚动列表，播报各个监测点的超标预警。
（注：版式安排上，我不希望看到那个深色讲干酪窖的档案页那种单列纵向死板居中的排布，也别弄成那个带一堆红蓝彩色标签的新闻门户那种左边多列瀑布流、右侧固定边栏的常见套路。我们只要最清爽现代的后台结构：左侧固定的菜单条，右边一大块留给灵活组合的数据卡片网格即可。）

**视觉**：
颜色的选择上，我看中了那个带有3D地形图和鲜艳粉橙色顶栏的页面——我们的主要数据监控场景就用它那种深色底搭配低饱和度的绿灰大地色，至于一些需要警示或特别强调的模块，可以穿插使用它里面那种大面积白底配大块鲜艳的粉红至蜜桃橙渐变色，对比会非常醒目。
字体的处理要参考那个偏米色背景、介绍自行车车架的网页。我想要那种讲究的质感：多用优雅的传统衬线体，把核心数据的大字号和底部的细小注脚字号拉开强烈的对比。甚至可以在左侧导航或大标题处，像它那样尝试一下罕见的竖排文字区块，增加一些设计深度。
虽然是个数据大屏，但我希望它给人的感觉能像那个车架网页一样，透出一种极度克制、安静的文艺气息，像是一本传统纸质档案或手工记录册，有一种从容不迫的匠人感，而不是那种让人看了觉得刺眼焦虑的监控台。
另外，数据卡片、表单输入框和按钮的做法，千万别做成最开头那个一堆彩色带有反光球体的拓扑图界面那样。那种带有强烈复古高光、多重渐变的3D质感球体，还有带明显内阴影的胶囊形按钮太油腻了。我这里只要最基础的扁平化处理，或者干净的细线框，最多加点极柔和的微投影即可。

**交互**：
图表区域支持鼠标悬浮展示具体时间节点的能耗刻度。上报表单在输入超阈值数据时需即时飘红提示。低于 768px 宽度时侧边栏需折叠为顶部汉堡菜单，所有横向网格自动重组为单列垂直滑动。

**验收**：
页面初始加载必须在2秒内完成；上报表单的必填项需经过严格的前端非空和数字格式校验；响应式断点切换时图表Canvas不可出现拉伸变形。

user_prompt_en:
**Overview**
This brief is for our upcoming digital year-end holiday greeting. We are sending this out to our top-tier industry partners, senior creatives, and enterprise clients. It cannot feel like a generic corporate e-card; it needs to be a crafted digital journey that respects their time and aesthetics. I want this to be an emotionally resonant piece that celebrates our shared milestones this year while setting a sophisticated tone for the next. The narrative should unfold slowly as they scroll, creating a moment of reflection in their busy inboxes. Our audience spends all day evaluating design and strategy, so the execution here must be flawless, concept-driven, and highly intentional.

**Page structure**
The flow needs to act as a singular, focused narrative thread. Therefore, keep the content in one single column scrolling down, no multiple columns at any point. We are guiding them through a specific story, step by step, and I don't want their eyes darting left and right.
*   **The Prologue (Hero):** A cinematic full-viewport opening. A subtle ambient background animation (perhaps slowly drifting abstract geometric snow or floating golden embers) with a gentle, welcoming headline: "A Season of Reflection." Underneath, a smaller subtitle: "Looking back at a year of momentum."
*   **The Journey (Data/Milestones):** We are professionals talking to professionals, so let's include some elegant data visualization reflecting our collective achievements. Three distinct scroll-triggered data blocks stacked vertically: "12 Global Campaigns Launched," "4 Million Lives Touched Through Design," and "1 Shared Vision." Each block needs ample breathing room.
*   **The Heart (Core Message):** A dedicated text section with maximum whitespace. The copy will read: "In a year defined by unprecedented velocity and shifting landscapes, your partnership has been our anchor. We wish you a quiet, restful holiday season, and a brilliant, inspired new year."
*   **The Gift (Interactive Element):** A stateful view where the user can interact. We will have a media block here. They can click to "ignite" a digital spark, which transitions the page state to reveal a personalized, handwritten-style signature from our executive team, alongside a bespoke audio chime.
*   **The Sign-off:** A minimal footer with our agency crest, standard copyright, and a subtle link to our main studio site, keeping the focus entirely on the message above.

**Visual**
This piece needs to carry a profound, restrained, and quiet energy. It should feel like stepping into a high-end art gallery exhibition — I want that exact deep, artistic aura that you get from the dark portfolio page with the ocean rocks. It needs to command attention through subtlety, not volume.

For the text treatments, I want to lean into that same dark portfolio page's approach to hierarchy. Give me those imposing, traditional serif fonts for the big headlines to provide a sense of gravitas and heritage, and then pair them with a highly legible, clean sans-serif for the secondary text and data points. This contrast is key to the editorial feel.

When it comes to the container shapes and interface elements, take a close look at the teal medical site. I want our media blocks and main content containers to have those exact large, generous rounded corners. If we have a trigger to play our recap video or audio, use that delicate circular wireframe button style they have. However, keep the utility links or navigation items at the very top as sharp, straight right-angle buttons, just like they did.

For the colors, I want to be very specific about what to avoid. I definitely don't want the stark white background, bright blue accents, and that massive, heavy pure black footer from the 'Bingo' team page. Similarly, stay far away from the dark grey-blue background and those aggressive, high-saturation neon pinks from that dashboard screenshot. Instead, let's ground our piece in a rich, velvety burgundy, paired with soft champagne gold text and subtle warm ivory accents to keep it festive but extremely elevated.

**Interaction**
The motion design must be deliberate, smooth, and respectful of the user's scroll speed.
*   **Entry:** A long, 2.5-second fade-in for the hero headline. It shouldn't just snap into existence; it should emerge from the background like a photographic exposure.
*   **Scroll progress:** As the user scrolls down through the single column, the data points in 'The Journey' section should fade in while slowly drifting upward (a gentle 30px parallax effect). The numbers should count up from zero to their final values using a smooth cubic-bezier easing curve, taking exactly 1.5 seconds to complete.
*   **The Spark (Stateful View):** In the 'Gift' section, the circular wireframe button should pulse subtly on a 3-second loop. When clicked, it triggers a seamless CSS state transition. The burgundy background in that specific block should gently bloom into a warmer crimson. Simultaneously, the executive signatures should draw themselves onto the screen using an SVG line animation. Once clicked, the button fades out permanently and is replaced by a soft "Thank You for 2024" text, locking that state so it feels like a completed, irreversible action.

**Acceptance**
*   The entire experience must be delivered as a single, self-contained HTML file containing all necessary CSS and JavaScript. No external asset dependencies other than standard web fonts (like Google Fonts) and embedded SVGs.
*   The single-column flow must remain strictly enforced across all breakpoints, from a 4K ultra-wide monitor down to a 320px mobile screen. Elements scale, but they never sit side-by-side.
*   The SVG drawing animations and number count-ups must only trigger once when their respective sections intersect the viewport (using Intersection Observer), ensuring the user actually sees the motion.
*   The primary color pairing (burgundy background, champagne gold text) must pass WCAG AA contrast standards for all reading text.

user_prompt_zh: 我们最近要推一个面向开发者的全新数据接口服务，项目代号叫青苔巷，目标是主打极简接入和高转化。现在需要一版首屏冲击力极强的API服务介绍页来做投放承接。整个页面的框架思路我希望参考后面那套浅色房源搜索页面的排布方式。具体来说，最顶部放一个干练的导航条，紧接着是一个带有大标题的视觉主图区用来抓眼球，主图下方横向平铺一排条件筛选栏，用来切换不同的API业务模块，再往下就是网格状排列的具体接口能力卡片。如果有开发者想看某个接口的详情，点击卡片后，要像那个房产网一样弹出一个多层级的居中大图弹窗，里面展示接口文档和调用示例。至于视觉的底子，这件事我已经提前敲定了，整页底色我要深的，字浮在深底上，绝对不能改，必须要这种深邃的技术氛围来镇住场子。在这个深色的基调上，文字的呼吸感和视觉跳跃非常关键。你看前面那个深色动物游戏界面的字是怎么处理的，我们要的就是那个方向。主标题必须要用加粗的大字号，配合带有明亮主题色也就是那种抢眼的橙黄色的无衬线字体，直接把用户的注意力死死钉在核心卖点上。其余的说明性文字都要处理得多为小字号，让层级跳跃大一些，偏向那种带点游戏感的极客风。不仅字要这样，区块的外观也要顺着这个深色游戏页面来。页面里的基础选项卡都做成带暗色描边的圆角矩形，一旦用户选中某个筛选条件或者激活某张卡片，边框要立刻变成亮橙色的粗边框，给足操作反馈。主推的动作按钮，比如页面最显眼的获取密钥，统统做成带有亮橙色渐变填充的胶囊形状，整体保持扁平，坚决不要任何阴影，就是要这种干脆利落的点击欲。接下来梳理一下具体的板块文案。导航条左边是青苔巷的品牌字样，右边放开发指南和登录入口。视觉主图区的大标题写下一代营销增长API引擎，副标题写一行代码接入，让你的产品长出营销大脑。横向的筛选栏设置成身份验证、用户画像、支付转化这几个核心模块。网格区根据选中的模块动态刷新，每张卡片上不仅要有接口名称，我还要在卡片的底部加入一个非常直观的进度条，作为完成度展示，用来向开发者暗示这个接口的接入进度，比如标上百分之八十五的竞品已集成，用这种功能钩子来制造一点FOMO情绪。这页要承载复杂的界面响应和数据可视化状态切换逻辑，弹出的居中大窗就是核心转化场，左侧必须是一个动态的代码高亮演示区，右侧是对应的参数说明。在筛选栏切换不同的类别时，下面的卡片网格需要带有一点交错出现的平滑过渡，不要干巴巴地一闪就变。页面最底部放一个强行动唤醒的横向区块，文案写今天就让业务跑在青苔巷基建上，再配一次那个胶囊按钮。我们要尽最大可能锁住用户的注意力，把流量都逼进转化路径里。

user_prompt_zh:
这个项目我们要打造的是一个沉浸式的专属健身计划和硬核训练记录页。你现在看到的这张参考图，那种过于干净、留白极大、仿佛默认 Bootstrap 框架出来的企业团队介绍页的感觉，正是我们要极力避免的。我需要你走向它的绝对反面。我们不要这种温吞的基础感，这个页面必须散发着汗水、粗犷和肾上腺素的味道，信息密度要高，要有一种让人一眼看过去就想立刻开始流汗的张力。因为这主要是在健身房里看的东西，所以一切设计的出发点必须是窄屏体验，移动端的呈现是重中之重，所有的滑动反馈和视觉爆发力都要在这个狭长的画幅里完成。

你再仔细看看截图里那些用来占位的团队成员头像，就是那些毫无边缘起伏、极度扁平和柔和的灰色圆块，这些感觉全都丢掉。在具体控件的刻画上，我要的是彻底的颠覆。不要任何圆润妥协的边缘，给我充满攻击性的锐利几何切角，或者是带有极强纵深感的厚重阴影和粗粝的边界线条。我们的卡片和按钮必须看起来有分量感，像是健身房里的杠铃片或者哑铃，按下去要有真实的物理下压反馈，而不是轻飘飘的纸片。

整个页面的叙事线从顶部的个人状态面板开始。这里不是简单的打个招呼，而是一个极具仪式感的模式切换区。文案方向要直接、煽动性强，比如用类似“今天，你想撕裂哪块肌肉？”这样的句子来破冰。这里需要一种深度的操作反馈，用户可以通过长按拖拽，在“增肌撕裂”和“极速减脂”两个主模式间来回切换。这个动作不只是换个字，还要瞬间联动底下所有模块的数据状态展示。紧接着是核心的数据可视化部分，我们要在这里铺一张本周训练肌群的动态热力图，或者是一个随手势滚动而不断生长攀升的训练强度心率曲线。绝不能用静态的死图，这个图表要在进入视线时带出复杂的视觉演变过程，能用极其鲜明的数据对比告诉用户哪天的训练最硬核。

往下走是每日训练清单的展示区。这里的操作体验需要做得非常深。每一个动作绝对不能是一行干瘪的字，而是充满力量感的可折叠模块。当用户点击某一个训练项目时，卡片需要以一种非常有张力的方式向下推开，露出里面的动作要领说明、组数记录表格以及一个用于动作演示的微型视频占位区。在记录每一组的重量和次数时，我希望看到类似拉动机械拨盘或者拖拽重力滑块的那种细腻操作感，当用户勾选完成一组训练时，整个模块要呈现一个充满成就感的视觉回弹，就像是完成了一次重击。除了训练本身，页面最后还要自然过渡到营养与恢复板块。这部分用一种偏向实验室或者营养配比仪器的感觉来呈现，三大项宏量营养素碳水、蛋白质和脂肪的摄入量，通过几个可以手指拖动调整的带刻度的试管状进度条来表示。整个页面的最终目标，就是让用户在这个极度聚焦的窄屏空间里，体验到一种强烈的自我重塑的史诗感。

user_prompt_en:
Hey, I'm setting up a local delivery ordering site for my new business called Bright Fold, and I need a functional, nice-looking page that isn't overly complicated to use.
- Start off the top with a massive, centered welcome area introducing our same-day local delivery, structured exactly like that first set of screenshots with the bright pink intro block.
- Below that intro, the page needs to expand into a full-screen ordering space, just like the second half of that same example, using a sidebar on the left for food categories and a really dense, multi-column wall of cards in the middle for the inventory.
- For the colors, pull them directly from that exact same design, using that unbelievably bright, high-saturation pink for the top welcome block to really grab attention.
- Once the user scrolls down to the ordering section, switch the background to that deep, dark grey they used, and use those bright blue and cyan gradients for the active cart numbers or selected items.
- The whole experience should feel totally loud, extroverted, and aggressively modern, capturing the exact same in-your-face energy as that pink and dark grey dashboard.
- Even with that loud energy, I want the text to look incredibly delicate, so use the letters from the screenshot with the white minimalist form and the mountain picture.
- Keep our main item descriptions small, tightly packed, and a muted grey color, but make all the menu headers super thin, all-caps, and really spaced out to keep it looking elegant.
- We need a clear section on the left sidebar letting people filter by groceries, hot meals, or pharmacy items so they can find things fast.
- The center area should display dozens of items at once so people can just click and add to their cart without having to open new pages.
- I really don't want the buttons or item boxes to look like the ones in the other examples, especially those gradient pill shapes or the weird clear wireframe buttons from the page with the male model photo.
- Also, definitely skip what that pale e-commerce page did with its items, where it's just raw square photos blending into the background with those harsh grey transparent boxes covering the corners.
- Instead, just make all our item boxes nice and clearly separated with soft rounded edges and a gentle shadow behind them so you know exactly where to tap, and use simple, chunky buttons for the add actions.
- Include a checkout slide-out panel on the right side that tallies up the delivery fee, the subtotal, and any driver tip before they finish.
- At the bottom, put a really clean payment form asking for the delivery address, phone number, and a huge box for gate codes or drop-off instructions.
- Make sure there is a quick re-order function for people who buy the same weekly groceries from Bright Fold over and over.
- One really important thing for my kitchen staff: we need to be able to print the daily orders out on A4 paper without it getting all garbled up, so make sure the page stays neat when it goes to a printer.
- Finally, add a tiny strip at the absolute bottom with our support email, operating hours, and a link to the refund policy.

ref_mix.label: A
ref_mix.looks_like: 包含亮粉色大色块引言区和深灰底色密集数据控制台两个截然不同的部分。

ref_mix.label: B
ref_mix.looks_like: 拼接了暗色山脉图文、白底极简表单和高饱和纯色背景物品网格。

ref_mix.label: C
ref_mix.looks_like: 上半部是鲜艳撞色的方块网格图，下半部是带复古大衬线字体的男模头图。

ref_mix.label: D
ref_mix.looks_like: 浅底色电商页，堆叠了大量带或不带半透明灰遮罩的无边框直角商品照片卡。

by_label.A: 包含两种截然不同的布局：前段为单列居中、带大面积色块的网页流，后段为铺满屏幕的后台仪表盘（包含侧边栏导航和多列密集的直角数据卡片墙）。
by_label.B: 包含居中的单列宽幅文本段落、居中窄栏宽的表单布局，以及无缝拼接的三等分纯色网格图片阵列。
by_label.C: 包含错落的无缝网格拼图布局（多种纯色方块拼贴），以及传统首屏居中文字叠加在大全景背景图上的单列布局。
by_label.D: 典型的电商卡片网格布局，包含横向均分的大幅无边框图文分类卡，以及多列整齐排列的正方形商品展示矩阵。

layout.why: 虽然 A 组整体组合很特殊，但其包含的“控制台网格”和“单列引言”是割裂的；如果模型只学到其单列部分，容易失去独特性造成判分困难。

by_label.A: 主打极高对比：前部大面积使用极高饱和度的亮粉色作为主视觉基底，后部仪表盘使用深灰暗底色，佐以蓝/青色渐变图表高亮。
by_label.B: 底色变化跳跃：包含带暗紫滤镜的深灰底色、大面积极简纯白表单底色，以及高纯度粉、黄、蓝纯色图块拼接。
by_label.C: 大面积高饱和撞色（明亮青、黄、粉、橙）占据主要视觉，辅以带渐变的深暗蓝底色区块和偏暖暗色调的照片背景。
by_label.D: 页面处于浅色高明度环境，主背景为纯白或浅灰，色彩几乎全部由低饱和度或复古色调的商品实拍照片提供。

palette.why: 第 1 份中极其抢眼且大面积的亮粉色铺底（且配白字）在其余三份中完全不存在，特征极度鲜明。

by_label.A: 以常规和偏粗字重的无衬线体为主，包含加粗的导航Logo和常规紧凑的控制台数据展示小字。
by_label.B: 大面积使用极细、轻薄的无衬线字体。正文密集体积小、颜色偏灰暗；表单标题为极细全大写且字间距明显拉宽，给人极简纤细感。
by_label.C: 字体风格混搭：既有非常粗旷醒目的红色无衬线大号副标，又有古典优雅、笔画粗细对比强烈的特大号经典衬线体头图标题。
by_label.D: 典型的标准层级无衬线排版，深黑色细体说明文字配合稍微加粗的分类大写标题，无夸张的字重或字号反差。

typography.why: 第 2 份极致纤细、宽字距的浅色排版具有辨识度，但如果模型还原时不够“极端”，很容易退化成与 D 份相似的常规偏细无衬线体。

by_label.A: 没有明显的引导点击按钮，后台面板包含紧凑的深色直角数据图表卡片及极细的深暗色分割线。
by_label.B: 包含纯白底色的矩形表单输入框，线条极细且颜色极浅，无阴影无背景圆角，呈现去组件化的极简风。
by_label.C: 具有红粉渐变填充的胶囊状（全圆角）实心按钮，以及无填充仅带有白色极细描边的全直角透明线框按钮。
by_label.D: 大面积使用无边框无阴影的直角图片充当卡片主体，部分图片上叠加了边缘锐利的半透明暗灰/冷灰色文字遮罩色块，以及黑底白字的极简直角小标签。

component.why: C 的胶囊/线框双形态按钮，与 D 的实图叠加半透明灰色硬角遮罩的卡片样式，均特征明确且完全不重叠，非常容易排查界定。

by_label.A: 张扬且充满视觉冲击力，情绪外放、热烈且现代感十足。
by_label.B: 冷峻、理性、严谨克制，具有高度的专业感与数据驱动氛围。
by_label.C: 极致的安静、空灵与放松，情绪高度克制且轻盈无压迫感。
by_label.D: 前卫、潮流、古灵精怪，带有波普艺术般的俏皮与拼接设计感。

atmosphere.why: 图1-3呈现的张扬热烈感与图4-6的严密冷峻、图7-9的空灵极简、图10-12的波普前卫截然不同，四者的情绪调性分别走向了完全不同的四个极端，极易辨认。
