user_prompt_en:
**Overview**
We need a diagnostic panel for database slow queries. The goal is to let DevOps engineers quickly identify, filter, and inspect underperforming SQL execution plans without wading through raw logs. This tool will significantly reduce the time our team spends troubleshooting production bottlenecks, so it has to be highly functional and easy to parse.

**Page structure**
Start with a top global navigation bar that includes breadcrumbs and a user profile indicator. Right below that, place a unified control bar containing environmental toggles to switch between Staging and Production databases. For the main display, I want the content area split into two side-by-side columns. The left side should house a dense, scrollable list of flagged queries showing the timestamp, database name, and execution duration. The right column will serve as the detailed inspection view.

**Visuals**
Keep the containers and inputs incredibly minimal, just like the blocks on that giant-text portfolio site — practically ditch the standard background color fills for the data modules, and just use extremely light, fine borders for the few sections that actually need bounding boxes. For the text, look at the first few shots of that dark dashboard. I want text handled exactly like they did it: a standard sans-serif where the hierarchy relies mostly on medium font weights and varying shades of text color, rather than jumping between extreme font sizes. Keep the text size contrast moderate just like they have it.

**Core functionality**
The unified control bar needs input fields for start date, end date, and minimum execution time in milliseconds, along with a primary action button to apply these filters. The right-hand detailed inspection view must include a pre-formatted text block for the actual SQL statement and a utility button to copy the query to the clipboard. We also need a simple pagination control at the bottom of the left column to handle large log outputs without freezing the viewport.

**Acceptance**
- The two-column layout must be strictly enforced on desktop monitors (1024px and up).
- On smaller screens, the layout must stack gracefully, with the list appearing above the detailed inspection view.
- All filter form fields must have visible focus states to ensure keyboard accessibility.
- The deliverable must be contained entirely within a single HTML file.

user_prompt_en:
**Overview**: We are launching the digital edition for the latest issue of our independent magazine, "Slow Tuesday". The aesthetic demands a strict minimalist ascetic approach, elevated through precise spacing rhythm and complex stateful interactions for the editorial spreads.

**Page structure**: The spatial hierarchy needs to be blocked out exactly like the site with the dark form section at the bottom. Start the hero with text on the left and a dark featured card on the right. Below that, drop into a three-to-four column grid of white, rounded cards for the article index, and finish the page with a dark, horizontally split form area for newsletter subscriptions.

**Visual**: To offset the ascetic feel, pull the colors from that purple portfolio page: a deep purplish-blue primary backdrop punctuated by vibrant orange, pink, and cyan graphic accents for active states. One passing note—looking at the page with the pricing table, I absolutely hate how cold that pure sans-serif setup feels with its massive bold titles and tiny, cramped body text. I strictly want an elegant, high-contrast serif for headings and a spacious slab-serif for reading blocks instead. Also, all interactive buttons must be fully rounded pills.

**Interaction**: The article index needs a stateful view expansion. Clicking a card seamlessly morphs it into a full-screen reading modal without a hard reload. Component consistency across these micro-interactions is critical.

**Acceptance**:
* Transition animations between the index grid and reading views maintain stable framerates.
* The three-to-four column grid collapses logically to a single column on mobile.
* All buttons are implemented as fully rounded pills.
